title: Event-decorator patterns for resumable streaming chat and idempotent retries
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Background: Engineers building chat UIs want a small, composable surface for streaming chat completions that: 1) exposes fine-grained events (token/chunk/delta/meta), 2) makes it straightforward to checkpoint/resume after transient failures, 3) provides a clear semantic for idempotent retries (so duplicate tokens are not shown), and 4) plays nicely with user-level middleware (eg. filters, rate limiters, telemetry wrappers).

Problem: Existing SDK patterns we have explored (streaming iterators, event adapters, and checkpoint hooks) cover many needs but feel orthogonal to a middleware-first developer experience. Users end up writing boilerplate to translate raw events into application-level replayable state. We need a lightweight, composable "event-decorator" API that sits between the low-level event stream and higher-level consumer callbacks.

Goal: Deliver a Python SDK API and reference implementation that: 
- Provides decorator-style middleware that can annotate, filter, and checkpoint the event stream.
- Supports deterministic resumability using a compact checkpoint token (not full conversation tape).
- Defines idempotent retry semantics and a small helper for merging duplicate deltas when replays occur.
- Includes examples: a minimal chat UI snippet, a server-side consumer that persists checkpoints, and a middleware that strips system tokens for TTS pipelines.

Non-goals: Building a complete persistence layer or long-term conversation store. This ticket focuses on the SDK surface, patterns, and a reference implementation using in-memory / s3 checkpoint storage examples.

Design notes: 
1) Event envelope: each streamed item from the runtime will be normalized to an envelope with fields: "type" (token|delta|meta|end), "seq" (monotonic counter string), "model_ts" (optional), "content" (string or structured), "checksum" (short checksum of content). The envelope shape is internal to the SDK and is not nested beyond primitive fields.

2) Decorator API: implement a decorator type "@event_decorator" that wraps async generators. Decorators accept an async generator of envelopes and yield transformed envelopes. Decorators should be composable via function composition: decorated = deco3(deco2(deco1(stream))).

3) Checkpointing: provide optional checkpoint hooks that consume the last-seen seq and checksum and produce a compact token (base64 of "seq:checksum:version"). Resume API accepts token and requests the server to replay from seq+1. The SDK helper will reconcile overlapping tokens by comparing checksums and using idempotent merge rules (trim duplicate prefixes).

4) Retry semantics: define two modes: "at-most-once UI" (client filters duplicates) and "exactly-once best-effort" (SDK attempts de-duplication using content checksums + seq heuristics). Document trade-offs and recommended defaults (P0: default to at-most-once UI).

Acceptance criteria: 
- New public API: event_decorator, make_checkpoint(), resume_from_checkpoint(token).
- Reference implementation in SDK that uses an in-memory checkpoint store and a second example using S3 presigned put/get.
- Unit tests covering: decorator composition, checkpoint serialization, resume merging of overlapping sequences, and retry modes.
- Two user-facing examples in docs: a minimal chat client and a TTS preprocessor middleware.
- Telemetry: emit event counts and checkpoint frequency to our metrics client (counter tags: decorator_name, checkpoint_result).

Out of scope for this ticket: TS/Go SDK parity (follow-up), runtime-level replay endpoints (assume backend supports replay by seq), and UI components.
steps: Design review: capture API shape + examples (this ticket)
Prototype: implement decorator helpers + in-memory checkpoint store in py-sdk branch
Tests: unit tests for composition, resume/merge, and retry modes
Docs: add 2 examples in SDK docs + code snippets
PRs: 1 implementation PR, 1 docs PR, add integration test against replay-enabled dev runtime
comments: 2026-03-10 - Aisha Kapoor: Created ticket with initial design proposal. Linked prototype notes: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1-example-event-decorator-proposal

2026-03-11 - Daniel Kim: Spike completed — implemented basic decorator that logs envelopes and yields unchanged events. Branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-py-sdk/tree/feat/event-decorator-spike
2026-03-12 - Mei Chen (PM): Suggested making checkpoint tokens forward compatible (add version int). Added to design notes.

2026-03-13 - Daniel Kim: Implemented checkpoint token helper and resume merging. Found edge-case where server replay includes a partial tokenized delta; added checksum compare to trim duplicate prefixes. Unit test added: tests/test_resume_merge.py
2026-03-14 - Security review (note): checkpoint tokens contain checksum only and no PII; flagged for accidental log redaction. Created follow-up ENG-334890 to add automatic redaction in telemetry.

2026-03-14 - Aisha Kapoor: Reviewed code and left feedback on PR: ensure decorator API exposes a synchronous helper to wrap sync consumers; request for ergonomic alias names (as_event_middleware, checkpoint_every).
risks: Resume token mismatch if backend changes seq semantics — will version tokens and include post-deploy migration notes
Telem overload — avoid emitting per-token metrics by default; sample 1/100 tokens unless decorator opts-in
User confusion between at-most-once and exactly-once modes — docs required with examples
acceptance_criteria: Public API implemented: event_decorator, make_checkpoint, resume_from_checkpoint
Unit + integration tests covering resume merging and retry modes
Docs and two runnable examples added to py-sdk repo
PR reviewed and approved by SDK lead and PM
